inputs.scope: The already calculated operator relations, including their central signs, are incoming. This argument does not re-prove the Weil-index identities.

inputs: Central epsilon has order two; its represented action is minus identity on the nonzero characteristic-zero Schwartz space.
derivation: Use projected matrices U(x)=[[1,x],[0,1]], M(a)=diag(a,a^-1), W=[[0,1],[-1,0]], matching the displayed WU(b)W relation. Every upper-triangular determinant-one matrix [[A,B],[0,D]] is uniquely U(AB)M(A).

For C nonzero, [[A,B],[C,D]]=U(A/C)M(-1/C)WU(D/C). Multiplication gives entries A,C,D, and the determinant-one condition forces B=(AD-1)/C. Thus these parameters are unique and the two cells are disjoint.

The displayed U/M commutation and W/M relation move every M past U or W. Two W symbols separated by U(b) reduce to one W when b is nonzero, using the displayed WU(b)W relation, and to zero W when b=0 using W². Scalar signs become a central epsilon power. Inverses of U,M,W reduce by these same relations. Induction on W count gives the two displayed word forms.

The unique projected parameters imply a word in the projection kernel reduces to 1 or epsilon. The represented epsilon is not the identity, since minus identity differs from identity on the nonzero characteristic-zero space. Therefore this kernel has exactly two elements.
